problem_text:
A logistics manager is allocating cargo containers for shipment. Available containers are:
* Container 1: volume 16 m³, revenue $21
* Container 2: volume 35 m³, revenue $112
* Container 3: volume 37 m³, revenue $181
* Container 4: volume 13 m³, revenue $89
* Container 5: volume 19 m³, revenue $283
* Container 6: volume 35 m³, revenue $103
* Container 7: volume 28 m³, revenue $64
* Container 8: volume 45 m³, revenue $141
* Container 9: volume 25 m³, revenue $121
* Container 10: volume 5 m³, revenue $199
* Container 11: volume 26 m³, revenue $86
* Container 12: volume 50 m³, revenue $220
* Container 13: volume 35 m³, revenue $260
* Container 14: volume 7 m³, revenue $145
* Container 15: volume 28 m³, revenue $192
* Container 16: volume 24 m³, revenue $214
* Container 17: volume 23 m³, revenue $220
* Container 18: volume 43 m³, revenue $143
* Container 19: volume 1 m³, revenue $116
* Container 20: volume 30 m³, revenue $197
* Container 21: volume 14 m³, revenue $57
* Container 22: volume 21 m³, revenue $16
* Container 23: volume 25 m³, revenue $224
* Container 24: volume 14 m³, revenue $227
* Container 25: volume 16 m³, revenue $224
* Container 26: volume 21 m³, revenue $69
The cargo vessel has a maximum capacity of 445 m³. Select the container combination that maximizes total revenue without exceeding this volume limit. Each container is either fully loaded or not loaded.
